parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is not the local low-risk reputation. National binary document/visa screening, federal facility restrictions, hostile custody practice, and criminal enforcement elsewhere remain in force and can reach visitors. A trans adult alone faces refusal, prolonged screening, outing at security, arrest, or birth-sex custody; a travelling family or minor adds care, school, and documentation exposure. Courts and local protections are partial, slow, and overridden by national action.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas: binary marker policy, X elimination for new issues, discrepancy refusal, possible permanent fraud finding for wilful misrepresentation; foreign advisories follow citizen detentions; airport secondary screening and pat-downs.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; litigation and legal-aid guidance; some courts block orders. No documented traveler-facing border protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can trigger secondary screening, interrogation, refusal/removal, and possible immigration detention, linking entry to custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopts conversion-therapy practices, hair cutting, hormone removal, care denial; facility arrest led to 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Habeas/civil-rights litigation exists, but hostile policies are enforced and data stopped. Not shown to protect detained trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or facility encounters can become investigation/detention; birth-sex placement and care withdrawal sharply raise abuse severity.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; many state/province bans, some criminal trespass; the seat has a national-attached ban and activist arrests; scope/enforcement partly uncertain.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Seat has no local ban and a low-risk ranking; some jurisdictions lack bans or have anti-discrimination law. National override makes reliability uncertain.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airports, courts, schools, transit, and government buildings can require sex-marker verification; refusal/departure can escalate to arrest and outing.

care_services.exposure: For minors: national framing of care as mutilation, school investigation/prosecution, funding bars, and many state bans likely deny visiting care. Adult medication continuity is not directly documented.
care_services.protection: No documented safe care pathway for trans visitors; some court injunctions may exist. Local protective reputation is overridden by national actions.
care_services.interaction: A parent seeking refills, school accommodation, or emergency care may be forced to disclose gender history to officials or staff, risking denial and outing.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive and counterterrorism language frames radical or pro-transgender agendas as domestic terrorism; official removal of trans materials; majority polls support binary documents; state criminalization remains in some jurisdictions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment-discrimination and hate-crime law, plus some local protections, remain on books; courts sometimes intervene. These are not reliable traveler protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing can encourage stops, refusals, harsher policing, and reduced willingness to report incidents; enforcement of hostile facility rules increases exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor travelling with an adult faces school and medical hostility, marker mismatch, care denial, and forced disclosure; an adult trans parent with a child may face document or activity screening.
minors_guardians.protection: No guardian-specific sanctuary documented; local protective ranking may reduce some street-level risk but cannot override national document, facility, or custody rules.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel can convert school enrollment, medical care, facility use, or border checks into official investigations, outing, or denial of support.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented visitor-specific hate-kill rate or trans-predation pattern, but official hostility, criminal facility enforcement, polls, and weak local bias statutes imply harassment/service-denial risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and some state/province bias laws exist, but coverage is partial and enforcement for trans visitors is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police calls during facility disputes or harassment can route to birth-sex custody or immigration screening rather than protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknown scope/enforcement of the seat ban, local police practice, private accommodation friction, exact detention triggers, and whether orders are currently blocked or operative. Unknowns are traveler-relevant here.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, legal-aid guidance, civil-liberties unions, and courts can sometimes relieve. Remedies are slow, jurisdiction-dependent, and do not neutralize border/federal exposure.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcome depends on timing, consulate access, lawyer availability, and which national measure is active; unresolved questions raise risk rather than indicate safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar traveler-facing border/visa exclusion for document and gender mismatch. This case is somewhat worse due airport outing, national facility exclusion, criminal bathroom enforcement elsewhere, and severe immigration/corrections custody; local low-risk ranking gives only partial offset.

Comparable birth-sex custody placement, care denial, and criminalized facility access. Less systematic organised sweeps or flogging/death risk, and functioning courts plus local protective law provide partial mitigation, so it sits slightly above the worst custody-only 0.25 pattern but remains severe.

Rated below routine-checkpoint cases because the dossier documents actual criminal arrest, birth-sex detention, hostile custody practice, and national exclusion policies, not merely district discretion. Elevated-risk anchors are too optimistic for the combined regime.

parsed.synthesis: Local low-risk status mitigates only if the visitor avoids federal facilities and border/custody touchpoints; entry screening, federal facility rules, corrections/immigration practice, and possible criminal enforcement remain operative. Adult travellers face refusal, prolonged screening, arrest, or harmful custody if outed. Travelling with a minor adds school, care, and documentation exposure. Remedies exist but are slow and jurisdiction-dependent.
